content.content:
=== V5 ===
-- Invoices carry a payment status so a project's detail page can show UNPAID/PAID and mark one paid.
-- New invoices default to UNPAID; existing rows adopt the same default via the column default.
ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNPAID';
=== V9 ===
-- Invoices now move through a lifecycle: DRAFT -> SENT -> PAID. A freshly raised invoice starts as a
-- DRAFT (it is sent later, which is what records an audit entry and unlocks payment), so the column
-- default becomes DRAFT. Existing rows keep whatever status they already hold.
ALTER TABLE invoices ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'DRAFT';

content.text:
The test passes.

## Summary

The change request was: "The money I am owed should only count invoices I have actually sent. Do not count drafts."

**Root cause:** The dashboard's outstanding-total logic filtered invoices by `status == "UNPAID"` — a status that no longer exists in the invoice lifecycle. Since migration V9, invoices move through `DRAFT → SENT → PAID`, so the outstanding figure was computed against a dead status value.

**Fix:** A single, local server-side change in `DashboardGetLogic.java` — the outstanding total now sums only invoices with `status == "SENT"`, which correctly excludes both drafts (not yet sent) and paid invoices (no longer owed). The accompanying Javadoc was updated to reflect the new rule.

No schema migration or front-end change was needed:
- Status is a free-text `VARCHAR(16)` with no CHECK constraint, so `SENT`/`DRAFT`/`PAID` already store fine.
- The `/__test__/seed` support already accepts an explicit `status` per invoice.
- The front-end already renders `dashboard-outstanding-total` from the `/api/dashboard` value.

The Playwright acceptance test passes: the seeded SENT invoices (100 + 200) total `$300.00`, while the DRAFT (50) and PAID (30) invoices are excluded.
